28/S0.subgoal: Describe the scope of the lecture on visual perception and its relation to displays.

28/S1.subgoal: Compare the structure and optical properties of the human eye and an engineered lens setup.

28/S2.subgoal: Calculate the combined optical power of the natural eye and explain how it focuses faraway objects.

28/S3.subgoal: Describe the principle of how VR headsets use engineered lenses to create the perception of an infinite image.

28/S4.subgoal: Explain how field of view and stereoscopy contribute to depth perception.

28/S5.subgoal: Define degrees of freedom and classify the types of motion perceived in a virtual world.

28/S6.subgoal: Determine how human physiological properties dictate the engineering requirements for VR displays.

28/S7.subgoal: List and describe the three primary technical considerations for designing effective VR displays (spatial, intensity, and temporal resolution).

28/S8.subgoal: Explain the effects of low spatial resolution, such as aliasing and the screen door effect.

28/S9.subgoal: Compare the traditional retina display concept with the higher resolution requirements for close-contact VR and AR headsets.

28/S10.subgoal: Identify methods, such as foveated rendering, used to mitigate visual artifacts like aliasing in VR.

28/S11.subgoal: Explain the importance of high frame rates for perceiving motion smoothly in immersive environments.

28/S12.subgoal: Summarize how visual perception influences the design of Extended Reality (XR) systems.
